doc.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

chapter: Reflections on Hamilton and the band
title: Emerson Brown as bandleader
summary: Brown was a dogmatic but helpful leader; the band's success owed to him, Donny and the drummers.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Tell me a little bit about playing with Emerson and what was he like back then?

Emerson I always thought was an excellent leader. He was a very dogmatic guy — a my way or the highway kind of guy — very much in control, which I think is good in a leader. Certainly as a young guy who’d never done this kind of stuff before it was very helpful to be told what to do and how to do it and all of that. Emerson was also very nice to me. He helped me with some of my studies and I always — when you’re sort of new and unknown and somebody helps you get over the rough spots you always remember those people. Emerson could be a very difficult person to work with. He was not always the friendliest person and he could be downright mean at times. And yet because he had helped me out so much as a freshman I always thought of that and then you know, sometimes when he was a jerk — he really isn’t, he’s a good guy, he’s just doing that. So

I thought he was a great leader and I think a lot of the success of the band was due to his musical leadership, to Donny’s wonderful ability to do all the behind the scenes stuff, and to these just killer drummers who just drove us at these tempos that would just knock your socks off. So I think those three things had a lot to do with it.
